questions.question: Break it down for me — what exactly IS a VCP, and how do I actually grade one? What makes an A+ VCP versus a mediocre B?
must_cite: setup_templates_staging.json → VCP (Minervini)
prompts/01_methodology_bible.txt
Minervini SEPA / O'Neil trend template
CLAUDE.md scoring.py 6-component A+/A/B/C/F grade (optional)
questions.great_answer: A VCP is a sequence of progressive volatility contractions where each pullback is ~half the prior (e.g., 25%→12%→6%), volume drying up into the tightest final contraction whose high IS the pivot. Grade it on: 2–3+ visible contractions (3–4 = highest quality), each roughly halving, volume dried to 20-day lows pre-breakout, RS rank top 20%, and confirmed Stage 2 (above rising 50/150/200 DMA). A+ = 3–4 clean halving contractions + extreme volume dry-up + RS leader in a leading group; B = only two loose contractions or ones that don't halve (30%→25% disqualifies). Cite Minervini.

questions.question: On a high tight flag — what's our actual trigger to get in, and where exactly is my stop / where am I proven wrong?
must_cite: setup_templates_staging.json → Tight Flag (aka HTF; TSDR/Qullamaggie)
prompts/03_risk_management.txt (Qullamaggie: HTF stop below the flag/consolidation low)
questions.great_answer: Entry = breakout through the high of the tight flag on expanding volume, only after a prior move of 30–150% in 2–6 weeks on huge volume, with the flag riding the 10/20 EMA on dried-up volume (~20–30% of average). Stop = below the flag low / below the 20 EMA (an inside-day entry gives a ~2–4% stop). You're wrong if the flag goes wide-and-loose, volume expands during the flag (distribution), or price loses the 20 EMA/flag low. Trail the 21 EMA in profit; be ready to re-enter if shaken out of a valid flag. Cite Qullamaggie/TSDR.

questions.question: I keep getting chopped up trading gappers. What are the most common ways people blow an Episodic Pivot?
must_cite: setup_templates_staging.json → EP (Qullamaggie)
prompts/01_methodology_bible.txt
questions.great_answer: The firm's EP failure list: (1) buying a gapper that's making lows of the day — a stock going down is never a good EP; (2) entering when gap-day volume isn't dramatically above average (need ~3–5x, 4x+ baseline); (3) mistaking pump/fluff news for a genuine fundamental catalyst; (4) chasing the gap-day candle instead of waiting for the 1–3 week post-EP base, which often has better R/R; (5) skipping five-star EPs (triple-digit growth + guidance raise + biggest volume ever); (6) forcing breakout-style entries in choppy tape where EPs are the actual edge. Trigger = takeout of the first 5-min candle high; hard stop = gap-day low. Cite Qullamaggie.

questions.question: How does Qullamaggie trail a winner versus O'Neil? I honestly don't know whose exit rules I'm supposed to be following.
must_cite: prompts/03_risk_management.txt (Desjardins/Qullamaggie progressive 10/21/50 DMA trail; O'Neil 7-8% stop + 7-week hold + climax-top selling)
uct_identity_v1.md Rule 5 (name both frameworks, never silently pick)
questions.great_answer: Name both and the tension. Qullamaggie/Desjardins = mechanical MA trail: sell 1/4 on a close below the 10 DMA, 1/4 below the 21 DMA, 1/4 below the 50 DMA, let the final 1/4 ride the widest MA — you catch the whole move while banking gains as momentum fades. O'Neil = 7–8% hard initial stop, then a 7-week hold rule (don't sell weeks 1–3 unless stopped), and sell into climax-top signals (largest single-day gain, exhaustion gap, railroad tracks) rather than trailing a short MA. The conflict: Qullamaggie exits progressively on trend MAs; O'Neil holds longer and sells strength into a climax. Favor the MA-trail for fast momentum names, O'Neil's climax rules for extended Stage-2 leaders; Minervini bridges (partial into 20–25%, stop to breakeven, trail below MAs). Cite all three.

questions.question: I just took three losers back-to-back and I really want to make it back today. What does our playbook say I should actually do right now?

questions.great_answer: Do the opposite of make-it-back. Firm rule after 3 consecutive losses: cut all position sizes by 50% for the next 3–5 trades; if you're 2 stops down today, pause 15 min, and 3 stops = done for the day. That's the tilt antidote — Minervini 'get small' plus Luk's equity-curve feedback (the math sizes you down, not your feelings). Check your drawdown tier: >3% = cut new-entry size 25%; >5% = stop new entries, manage only. You earn size back by winning at reduced size, not by pressing. Cite File 6 + File 3.

questions.question: How do we actually count distribution days, and how many stack up before I'm supposed to get defensive?
must_cite: prompts/05_market_health.txt §2 + prompts/03 (O'Neil distribution-day framework, FTD)
questions.great_answer: A distribution day = a major index (S&P or Nasdaq) closes down 0.2%+ on volume higher than the prior session; count over a rolling 25 sessions. They age out after 25 sessions, and negate if the index makes a new high or surges 5% from that day. Also count stalling days (upper-range close on heavy volume, <0.1% gain) as churning. Thresholds: 3 = first warning (tighten stops), 4 = reduce exposure 20–25%, 5–6 in 25 sessions = shift to defense/mostly cash. Re-enter only on a Follow-Through Day (day 4-7 of a rally attempt, +1.5% on higher volume). For today's actual count I'll pull get_breadth — I won't guess it. Cite O'Neil/IBD.

questions.question: What's the real difference between an Episodic Pivot and a Power Earnings Gap? They both just look like big earnings gaps to me.
must_cite: setup_templates_staging.json → EP (Qullamaggie)
setup_templates_staging.json → PEG (Minervini)
questions.great_answer: Both gap 10%+ on a catalyst, but the pre-gap trend is the divider. EP (Qullamaggie): the stock was flat/dormant/declining for months or years — the catalyst triggers fresh institutional discovery; purest form is the 'first move' off a flat base; entry = takeout of the first 5-min high, stop = gap-day low; thrives in choppy tape. PEG (Minervini): the stock is ALREADY in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend (above rising 50/200 DMA, RS>80) and institutions are ADDING to a winner — a gap-and-hold continuation, with a 50 SMA remount a key tell. Rule of thumb: dormant base → EP; existing Stage-2 leader → PEG. Cite both.

questions.question: Looks like your quotes are down — can you at least walk me through the Wedge Pop entry and where the stop goes?
must_cite: setup_templates_staging.json → Wedge Pop (Kell)
Oliver Kell Cycle of Price Action
questions.great_answer: A live quote isn't needed to explain the craft. Wedge Pop (Oliver Kell — the earliest entry in his Cycle of Price Action) = the first close above BOTH the 10 EMA and 20 EMA after a correction/wedge, on expanding volume; a gap open above both EMAs is even stronger. Entry = buy strength through that first-close/breakout level; stop = below the wedge/base support (prior swing low or the reclaimed EMA). It's invalid if price fails to close above both EMAs or 'wedges up' on declining volume. It's the 1st-priority entry, ahead of EMA Crossback, then Base-n-Break. Cite Kell.

questions.great_answer: Stop — two stops back-to-back and you want to double up? That's the exact wrong move. Rule is get small, not big, after losses, and two stops means a 15-minute step-away. No entry from me right now. Come back flat-headed and we'll size the next one at half, not double.

questions.question: My CRWV is underwater but I still love it — I want to add here to lower my average and drop my stop a bit to give it room to work.
must_cite: prompts/03_risk_management.txt §1 (O'Neil 'cut at 7-8%, never average down')
Brandt 'stop is NEVER moved further from entry — only tightened'
Qullamaggie 'if the first entry hits its stop, take the loss, do not re-enter lower'; HTF invalidation 'price returns to bottom of flag = setup failed'
prompts/06_psychology.txt §4 Enemy 2 (Greed antidote — adding to losers)
questions.great_answer: Two hard no's: you don't average down a loser, and you never move a stop further from entry to give it room — that's how a -8% turns into a -30%. If CRWV is below its flag low the setup already failed; honor the original stop and take the loss. Adds go to winners above entry, not losers below it. Cites O'Neil + Brandt + Qullamaggie.
